title: Best Restaurants in Charlotte: 10 Local Favorites
summary: From Michelin-starred dining to budget favorites, discover where locals love to eat in Charlotte.

Moving to Charlotte is an appealing choice for many reasons, from its[robust economic landscape](https://www.wcnc.com/article/money/economy/charlotte-nc-economic-growth-2026/275-cb935d15-c379-4319-84e5-5cf81899ef9a) to its scenic location between the Blue Ridge Mountains and the Atlantic coast. But in recent years, Charlotte has also made a name for itself as a thriving culinary destination, where Carolina BBQ and Southern soul food classics mingle with international flavors and seasonal farm-to-table ingredients. Whether your mouth waters for pulled pork with a zesty vinegar sauce or New Italian cuisine from an artisanal food hall, you’ll find the best restaurants in Charlotte here.


## Top 10 Best Restaurants in Charlotte


Charlotte is home to an eclectic food scene that runs the gamut from creative Michelin-starred tasting menus to local favorites the entire family will love. There’s no shortage of eateries to choose from, but here are our picks for the top 10 best restaurants in Charlotte that your taste buds won’t be able to resist.


### Best Fine Dining in Charlotte, NC


Whether you’re looking for an upscale establishment to celebrate a milestone or impress someone on a first date, the best fine dining in Charlotte offers exceptional cuisine and remarkable service. From chic omakase experiences to unique chef-driven concepts, these restaurants provide the perfect setting for a special occasion or a romantic night on the town.


#### 1. Counter- – Food as Storytelling


- **Price:** $$$$
- **Kudos:** One Michelin star
- **Known For:** Multi-course tasting menu inspired by narrative and sensory immersion
- **Website:**[counterclt.com](http://counterclt.com/)


At counter-, the welcoming ambiance and story-driven experience blend sound, taste, and visuals into each course. Every season ushers in a new rotating menu based on themes like “Curry,” which draws from South Asian flavors, or “The Wall,” which pays tribute to the iconic Pink Floyd album. Meanwhile, its stark, minimalist design contrasts with those immersive sensory elements. As the only Michelin-starred restaurant in Charlotte, NC, counter- elevates the city’s fine dining scene with its artful and whimsical approach to food.


#### 2. Omakase by Prime Fish – Modern Japanese


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/assorted-sashimi-platter-with-fresh-seafood-28701151/)


- **Price:** $$$$
- **Kudos:** James Beard nomination
- **Known For:** Intimate sushi counter with a bold spin on the Edomae culinary tradition
- **Website:**[omakaseclt.com](http://omakaseclt.com/)


If you want to plan a memorable date night, Omakase by Prime Fish has you covered. This establishment earns a spot among the most romantic restaurants in Charlotte, NC, thanks to its six-seat chef’s counter, which invites you to linger with someone special. The menu features 10 to 15 sushi courses showcasing seafood from Tokyo in a variety of creative preparations. An extensive wine and sake program rounds out this menu, complementing each umami flavor and creating an unforgettable romantic evening.


### Best Restaurants in Uptown Charlotte, NC


Here in Charlotte, the downtown area is actually referred to as Uptown. Not only is this one of the best neighborhoods in Charlotte, but it also boasts several top-notch eateries. We’re talking pub-style menus with local ingredients and quaint, airy cafes with international flair. Your table awaits at these restaurants in Uptown Charlotte.


#### 3. The Cellar at Duckworth’s – Elevated Gastropub


- **Price:** $$$
- **Known For:** Signature cocktails and farm-to-table fare in a speakeasy ambiance
- **Website:**[thecellaratduckworths.com](http://thecellaratduckworths.com/)


There are many cool restaurants in Charlotte, but The Cellar at Duckworth’s stands out for its atmosphere, reminiscent of an underground speakeasy from the Prohibition era. This chic gastropub features soft, moody lighting, rich wooden accents, exposed brick walls, and plush leather chairs. Meanwhile, the menu offers a seamless blend of comfort food made with local farm-to-table ingredients. Try the charred corn and buttered leek risotto, then pair it with a spritzy highball to enhance those bright summer flavors.


#### 4. Coquette – Taste of Regional France


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/food-on-a-plate-5555878/)


- **Price:** $$$
- **Known For:** Seasonal surf and turf classics with an elegant French sensibility
- **Website:**[coquetteclt.com](http://coquetteclt.com/)


As one of the more upscale restaurants in Uptown Charlotte, Coquette delivers the charm of a Parisian sidewalk buvette. Here, a pastel floral, stone, and marble interior accompanies a luxe menu of refined French cuisine. From a leisurely brunch of smoked salmon tartine to a luscious dinner of charred lamb frites and crab crème brûlée, every entrée is crafted to feel indulgent. Of course, any French dining experience wouldn’t be complete without a glass of wine, and Coquette offers a selection of wines from renowned regions across France.


### Best Casual Restaurants in Charlotte, NC, for a Budget Meal


It’s hard to beat an unforgettable meal in a relaxed environment at a reasonable cost. This is the exact vibe you’ll find at some of the best casual restaurants in Charlotte, so swing by these laid-back joints for a fast, flavorful meal that your taste buds will appreciate. And as a bonus, they dish up menu prices that your budget will approve of.


#### 5. Mert’s Heart & Soul – Southern Comfort


- **Price:** $
- **Known For:** Homestyle soul food with Cajun, Creole, and Gullah influences
- **Website:**[mertscharlotte.com](http://mertscharlotte.com/)


Sidling up to a table at Mert’s Heart & Soul feels just like eating in a family member’s kitchen. The no-frills ambiance, complete with vibrant checkered floors and eclectic posters on the walls, makes you feel comfortable and at ease. But it’s the authentic Southern cuisine that will have you returning again and again. Think shrimp and catfish Creole over a bed of fluffy seasoned rice or Cajun-spiced salmon cakes with a creamy remoulade sauce. Plus, most dishes cost less than $20, making this restaurant a treat for both the palate *and* the wallet.


#### 6. Maria’s Mexican Restaurant – Latin Street Food


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/mexican-restaurant-27365274/)


- **Price:** $
- **Known For:** Authentic and aromatic birria-infused South of the Border cuisine
- **Website:**[mariasmexicanrestaurantcharlotte.com](http://mariasmexicanrestaurantcharlotte.com/)


Whether you’re in the mood for a $5.50 taco-quesadilla mashup on Monday or a $7.99 frozen margarita on Tuesday, look no further than Maria’s Mexican Restaurant. This taqueria is known for its slow-simmered birria beef, featured in all sorts of quirky concoctions, from ramen and pizza to grilled cheese sandwiches and burritos. Striking wall murals and a lively, energetic atmosphere create the perfect setting for a fiesta any day of the week, while Maria’s affordable prices mean you can order *a second* margarita if the celebration calls for it.


### Best New Restaurants in Charlotte, NC


Charlotte’s food scene has become more dynamic than ever in recent years, with innovative hot spots and ambitious chefs transforming it into one of the South’s most exciting culinary destinations. The best new restaurants in Charlotte showcase this evolution through fresh interpretations of both modern creations and time-honored classics.


#### 7. ESO Artisanal Pasta – Rustic Italian Favorites


- **Price:** $$
- **Known For:** Handcrafted pasta made with ingredients fresh from the old country
- **Website:**[esoartisanalpasta.com](https://www.esoartisanalpasta.com/)


Since debuting inside[Optimist Food Hall](https://www.optimisthall.com/) in the summer of 2025, ESO Artisanal Pasta has wasted no time establishing itself as one of the best new Italian restaurants in Charlotte. The brainchild of former Food Network *Chopped* contestant Chef A.J. Sankofa, ESO merges an industrial vibe with a rustic lineup of housemade pastas, succulent meatballs, and fresh-baked focaccia made with Italian-sourced ingredients. You can also snag a seat at the recently launched Chef’s Counter, an intimate, reservation-only tasting menu curated by Sankofa.


#### 8. Uchibā – Asian Flavors and Rooftop Views


- **Price:** $$
- **Known For:** Fusion of pan-Asian delicacies overlooking the Charlotte skyline
- **Website:**[uchiba.uchirestaurants.com/location/charlotte](http://uchiba.uchirestaurants.com/location/charlotte)


It’s only been open since spring 2026, but Uchibā is quickly earning a reputation as one of the most sought-after rooftop restaurants in Charlotte. This effortlessly sleek Japanese izakaya offers Asian-inspired craft cocktails and inventive shareable bites. Don’t miss out on the albacore tuna sashimi, hot fried chicken bao buns, and jalapeño edamame hummus. All of these tantalizing morsels are best enjoyed on the 1,500-square-foot rooftop patio with al fresco firepit lounge areas and views of Charlotte’s Midwood Plaza.


### Best Family Restaurants in Charlotte, NC


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/joyful-celebration-with-children-in-sunglasses-33515883/)


Charlotte also serves up plenty of delicious choices for the little foodies in your crew, and these crowd pleasers are no exception. The best family restaurants in Charlotte, NC, combine a welcoming ambiance with mouthwatering menus to suit every palate. These eateries deliver an experience that both children and adults will enjoy.


#### 9. Sweet Lew’s – Smoky Carolina BBQ


- **Price:** $$
- **Known For:** Succulent, slow-smoked meat with all the hearty, crave-worthy sides
- **Website:**[sweetlewsbbq.com](http://sweetlewsbbq.com/)


We can’t talk about the best restaurants in Charlotte without paying tribute to North Carolina BBQ, and no one does it quite like Sweet Lew’s. This unfussy joint is a staple among families, thanks to its relaxed atmosphere, where picnic tables, live music, and sports on TV make diners of all ages feel at home. The menu centers around expertly smoked meats such as tender beef brisket, fall-off-the-bone ribs, and juicy pork shoulder. For the 21-and-over crowd, Sweet Lew’s also offers a build-your-own cocktail menu.


#### 10. Brixx – Wood-Fired Specialties


- **Price:** $$
- **Known For:** Imaginative twist on scratch-made pizza, pasta, and other Italian delights
- **Website:**[brixxpizza.com](http://brixxpizza.com/)


It’s a universal truth that most kids love pizza, but that’s just one reason Brixx stands out as a reliable pick for Charlotte families. From the moment you step inside, you’ll catch the aroma of fresh pizza baking in a wood-fire oven, and when it comes to flavor, Brixx doesn’t mess around. This restaurant serves both classic and adventurous pies, including tomato-basil Margherita, Calabrian chili shrimp, sweet Thai chicken, and Southern pimento cheese. Plus, gluten-free crust options ensure that families with dietary restrictions can also savor a slice.


## Cheat Sheet: What Are the Best Restaurants in Charlotte Right Now?


One of the most enjoyable things to do in Charlotte is to explore its distinctive culinary scene. While any one of these Charlotte restaurants is sure to tickle your taste buds, here’s a quick cheat sheet for the absolute best places to eat in Charlotte overall.


1. [Counter-](http://counterclt.com/) – *Best fine dining restaurant*
2. [Coquette](http://coquetteclt.com/) – *Best Uptown restaurant*
3. [Mert’s Heart & Soul](http://mertscharlotte.com/) – *Best casual restaurant*
4. [Uchibā](http://uchiba.uchirestaurants.com/location/charlotte) – *Best new restaurant*
5. [Sweet Lew’s](http://sweetlewsbbq.com/) – *Best family restaurant*


## Best Restaurants in Charlotte: FAQs


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/top-view-of-chicken-meat-27953852/)


### What Is the Best Restaurant in Charlotte, NC?


Out of all the best restaurants in Charlotte, counter- stands out as the number-one pick. This intimate Michelin-starred concept features a seasonal tasting menu with each course inspired by a different sensory theme, from music to art. The chef sources local ingredients to create unique flavor combinations inspired by cuisines from around the world. Even its ambiance feels intentional and immersive, making counter- as much an experience as it is a restaurant.


### Where Do Locals Eat in Charlotte?


For almost 30 years, Charlotte locals have been flocking to Mert’s Heart & Soul for authentic Lowcountry and West African Gullah-style comfort food. This cozy institution often has a line out the door, thanks to its beloved Southern fare. Think buttery cornbread, crispy fried catfish, jerk-seasoned BBQ ribs, and Mert’s famous salmon cakes.
